root.name: Pterodactyl Defense: Fianchetto, Queen Benoni Pterodactyl
root.moves: 1. d4 g6 2. c4 Bg7 3. Nc3 c5 4. d5 Qa5

overview: Black fianchettoes, plays ...c5 and sends the queen to a5 early, targeting c3 and e4. White gets space with d5 and then must handle ...Bxc3 or ...b5 breaks. Black's play is hypermodern and awkward to meet, but the early queen can be exposed.

white_ideas.idea: Build the centre with e4 and Nf3
Develop Bd2 and kick the queen

typical_structures.structure: Benoni-like pawn structure with queen on a5

character.notes: An uneven hypermodern fight with the black queen sortie.

sublines_that_differ.name: Pteranodon
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 g6 2. c4 Bg7 3. Nc3 c5 4. d5 Bxc3+ 5. bxc3 Qa5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black doubles White's pawns at the cost of the bishop pair.

character.reason: The early queen and unbalanced pawns give both sides tactical chances.

gambit.reason: Material is level and no pawn is offered.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose this set-up.

plans.reason: Black lets White take the centre and attacks it from the flanks.
